paper.title: Hydrogen Storage in Untreated/Ammonia-Treated and Transition Metal-Decorated (Pt, Pd, Ni, Rh, Ir and Ru) Activated Carbons

defaults.verified_by: Agent B (sonnet): 536 cells, 0 numeric disputes, all 28 Table-2 uptakes/uncertainties/temperatures confirmed and column alignment re-derived. Agent C adjudication: (1) N content 2.0 wt% nulled on the 6 metal-decorated ammonia-treated composites (measured on the ammonia-treated support only, section 3.1; not re-measured on the composite; HYC-0027-M3 precedent), kept only on S2; (2) calibration point added by hand (He skeletal-density void-volume correction, section 2) per tiering doc, lifting the 77 K rows C->B so all 28 rows are B; (3) metal impregnation removed from activation_method (not a pore-activation; HYC-0027 precedent).

notes.sa: this paper reports no numerical surface area for any sample; the textural data (a BET area improvement, an average micropore volume ~0.4 cm3/g that is ~half of a total pore volume ~0.8 cm3/g, and a ~2 nm micropore width) are approximate, given only in aggregate and cross-referenced to the authors' prior paper ref 90 (section 3.2), so surface_area_method=none and no pore volume is recorded
notes.metalload: metal decoration at a nominal 5.0 wt% target by ultrasound-assisted impregnation (section 2); the loading is the synthesis target, not independently quantified. EDX shows a platinum signal in every sample because platinum sputter-coating was used to remove surface charge (a preparation artifact), so EDX cannot confirm decorated-metal content
notes.ncon_support: the ammonia-treated AC support contains 2.0 wt% N by CHNS (section 3.1); on this metal composite the N content was not separately measured, so dopant_concentration is left empty while dopant_element=N records the ammonia-derived nitrogen
notes.ncon: nitrogen introduced by ammonia-gas treatment; 2.0 wt% N by CHNS elemental analysis (section 3.1); the ammonia also mildly erodes meso/macropores while leaving micropores unchanged
notes.type: uptake_type=excess (exact-word rule): all uptakes are evaluated as excess (Gibbs) gas adsorption quantities and Table 2 is headed 'excess hydrogen storage capacities'
notes.press: pressures are nominal: the 77 K value is the saturation maximum reached at ~7 bar (the excess isotherm declines with further pressure; several 298 K isotherms end near 90 bar) and the 298 K value is at ~100 bar (Table 2 column headers; 'from ambient to 100 bars', section 2); recorded as 7 and 100 bar
notes.incr: the Table 2 'Incremental wt.%' columns are percentage changes relative to the untreated/undecorated sample, not uptake values, and are not extracted
notes.method: excess H2 by volumetric Sievert method (HPVA-II, Micromeritics, to 200 bar); degassed 12 h at 200 C under vacuum, degassed mass used; specimen volume He-corrected via skeletal density (void-volume correction); 6N H2; sample mass >= 2.0 g; PCI curves repeated for repeatability; the ± values are identical across samples (0.1 at 77 K, 0.01 at 298 K) and the paper does not define them
notes.base: base carbon is commercial Norit RX 1.5 Extra activated carbon (CABOT); synthesis_method=commercial for every sample
notes.class: metal-decorated samples are class=composite with metal_element set (corpus convention HYC-0027/HYC-0029: a metal-bearing carbon is a composite); the undecorated base is activated_carbon and the undecorated ammonia-treated base is doped_carbon
notes.cal: calibration point awarded by hand (tiering doc l.24/l.73): section 2 describes the He skeletal-density void-volume correction
